```{r}
# clean and validate
# Convert eventDate into a standard date format
orcas_clean <- orcas %>%
  mutate(
    observation_date = as.Date(
      substr(eventDate, 1, 10),
      format = "%Y-%m-%d"
    ),
    year = year(observation_date),
    month = month(observation_date)
  )
```

1. Define the spatial research question
Research question: Does the global spatial distribution of recorded killer whale occurrences during summer remain consistent between 2015 and 2025?

Hypotheses
- H₀: The geographic distribution of recorded killer whale occurrences during summer does not differ substantially between years.
- H₁: The geographic distribution of recorded killer whale occurrences during summer changes between years.
One important decision: because summer occurs at different times in each hemisphere, define it as:
- Northern Hemisphere summer: June, July, August.
- Southern Hemisphere summer: December, January, February.

```{r}
# standardize summer: Southern Hemisphere summer crosses two calendar years. For example, December 2015–February 2016 is the 2015/16 summer. We will label it 2015, so it can be compared with Northern Hemisphere summer 2015.


orcas_summer <- orcas_clean %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(observation_date),
    !is.na(decimalLatitude),
    !is.na(decimalLongitude),
    between(year, 2015, 2026)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    hemisphere = if_else(
      decimalLatitude >= 0,
      "Northern",
      "Southern"
    ),

    summer_year = case_when(
      hemisphere == "Northern" ~ year,
      hemisphere == "Southern" & month == 12 ~ year,
      hemisphere == "Southern" & month %in% c(1, 2) ~ year - 1,
      TRUE ~ NA_integer_
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(
    (hemisphere == "Northern" & month %in% 6:8) |
    (hemisphere == "Southern" & month %in% c(12, 1, 2)),
    !is.na(summer_year),
    between(summer_year, 2015, 2025)
  )

# Built following Workshop 4 custom function standards to summarize annual metrics
summarise_orca_summer <- function(data_df, target_hemisphere) {
  # Safety check: ensure valid hemisphere argument is passed using stop()[cite: 90]
  if (!target_hemisphere %in% c("Northern", "Southern")) {
    stop("Error: target_hemisphere must be either 'Northern' or 'Southern'.")
  }
  
  data_df %>%
    filter(hemisphere == target_hemisphere) %>%
    group_by(summer_year) %>%
    summarise(
      record_count = n(),
      mean_latitude = mean(decimalLatitude, na.rm = TRUE),
      mean_longitude = mean(decimalLongitude, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}

# Test the custom function for both hemispheres
northern_summary <- summarise_orca_summer(orcas_summer, "Northern")
southern_summary <- summarise_orca_summer(orcas_summer, "Southern")

print("Northern Hemisphere Summer Summary:")
print(head(northern_summary))




#check summer records
#orcas_summer %>%
 # count(summer_year, hemisphere)

# nrow(orcas_summer)
```
summer filter has retained 13,036 occurrence records across 2015–2026
- Northern Hemisphere records are consistently higher than Southern Hemisphere records.
- Records increase substantially in 2024 and 2025.
- Southern Hemisphere records are particularly low in 2020, with only 19 records.

```{r}
northern_summary <- summarise_orca_summer(orcas_summer, "Northern")
southern_summary <- summarise_orca_summer(orcas_summer, "Southern")

print(northern_summary)
print(southern_summary)
```
- In the Northern Hemisphere, record counts surge from 278 in 2015 up to a peak of 1,897 in 2025.

- In the Southern Hemisphere, record counts are generally lower,with a jump from 64 in 2015 to a peak of 847 in 2025 and a notable dip to 19 in 2020, likely reflecting COVID-19 pandemic impacts on field monitoring and citizen science reporting.

- Northern Hemisphere Latitude: Remains remarkably stable, hovering tightly around ~54ºN to 56ºN every single year despite the massive increase in sample size. This supports spatial consistency in core monitoring regions.

- Northern Hemisphere Longitude: Shows a notable westward shift over time—moving from -72.6º (Western Atlantic/European waters) in 2015 down to -122º (Northeast Pacific / Pacific Northwest) by 2025. This provides a quantifiable metric to argue against complete consistency (H₁), highlighting how increased reporting platforms or shifting observation effort change spatial representation over time.

- Southern Hemisphere Latitude: Exhibits a slight southward shift from ~-50º in 2015 to ~-61º in 2025, reflecting an increasing concentration of records in higher-latitude polar or sub-polar waters over time.

- Southern Hemisphere Longitude: Exhibits high inter-annual volatility rather than a smooth directional trend—fluctuating between negative values concentrated in the South Atlantic and South American sectors and positive values in the Indian Ocean and Australasian sectors. This variability underscores how lower baseline recording effort and sporadic, expedition- or tourism-based reporting in remote southern waters can heavily influence spatial distribution metrics over time.

- Southern Hemisphere: Shows greater centroid volatility (e.g., longitude swinging heavily from positive values near Australia/Indian Ocean to deeply negative values near South America/Antarctica), largely driven by lower sample sizes and isolated expedition or tourist vessel reporting.

- Unlike the Northern Hemisphere, which showed a gradual westward longitude drift, the Southern Hemisphere mean longitude exhibited high inter-annual variability—shifting between negative values centered in the South Atlantic/South American sectors and positive values in the Indian Ocean/Australasian sectors. This volatility is largely driven by lower baseline recording effort and isolated expedition- or tourism-based reporting in remote southern waters."

```{r, echo=FALSE}
# for slide presentation, save plots to outputs folder

# 1. Combine both summaries and reshape into long format for faceting
combined_summary <- bind_rows(
  northern_summary %>% mutate(hemisphere = "Northern Hemisphere"),
  southern_summary %>% mutate(hemisphere = "Southern Hemisphere")
) %>%
  filter(between(summer_year, 2015, 2025)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(mean_latitude, mean_longitude), # Adjust column names if yours differ slightly
    names_to = "metric",
    values_to = "degrees"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    metric = recode(
      metric,
      "mean_latitude" = "Mean Latitude (°)",
      "mean_longitude" = "Mean Longitude (°)"
    )
  )

# 2. Plot trends over time
p_trends <- ggplot(combined_summary, aes(x = summer_year, y = degrees, colour = hemisphere)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  facet_grid(metric ~ hemisphere, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2015, 2025, by = 2)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Northern Hemisphere" = "lightblue", "Southern Hemisphere" = "skyblue")) +
  labs(
    title = "Spatial Shifts in Summer Killer Whale Distributions (2015–2025)",
    subtitle = "Annual mean latitude and longitude across hemispheres",
    x = "Summer Year",
    y = "Mean Coordinate (Degrees)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
    legend.position = "none",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

# Display and save
p_trends
ggsave("outputs/spatial_trends_summary.png", plot = p_trends, width = 11, height = 6.5, dpi = 300)
```

# Combine side-by-side by year for a compact comparison table

  northern_summary %>% filter(between(summer_year, 2015, 2025)),

  ),

)

  mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 1)))

# 2. Assign the presentation-ready column names directly by position

)

ggsave(
  "outputs/hemisphere_summary_table.png",

  width = 10,
  height = 4.5,
  dpi = 300
)
